newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish military denies north Iraq strike reports.
newsitem.headline: Turkish military denies north Iraq strike reports.

text.p: The Turkish military on Thursday denied news reports that it had launched cross-border strikes against separatist Kurdish rebels in northern Iraq.
But a cabinet minister was quoted as saying Turkey had asked Iraq for understanding over possible incursions into its territory to thwart Kurdish rebels.
"There is no question of such a thing at the moment," a high-ranking military official told Reuters, reacting to the Western news reports.

The Foreign Ministry also denied that Turkey had mounted air strikes against rebels of the separatist Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK), which uses northern Iraq as a base to launch attacks against Turkey.
Turkey said on Wednesday that PKK guerrillas had massed on its border in northern Iraq, where an Iraqi military incursion at the weekend prompted U.S. missile strikes against Iraq.
Witnesses in the southeastern Turkish city of Diyarbakir said they saw busloads of troops headed towards the border areaon Thursday and warplanes patrolled the skies.
Justice Minister Sevket Kazan told Anatolian news agency that Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan met Iraq's charge d'affaires in Ankara on Thursday.

"During these evaluations, we informed them that Turkey may cross the Iraqi border, that it may carry out certain operations there with the aim of preventing terrorist infiltrations in northern Iraq," the agency quoted Kazan as saying.
"We requested they show understanding towards these operations, which we will do because of necessity."
Kazan, from the Islamist wing of the coalition government, said the region had spun out of Iraq's control amid U.S. "interventions".

The United States launched cruise missiles against Iraqi military targets on Tuesday and Wednesday after Baghdad's forces joined a Kurdish faction in attacking the northern Iraqi regional capital of Arbil and ousting another Kurdish group.
Kazan said the U.S. strikes were as illegal as the Iraqi attacks.
